answer: Sybil resistance in the agent economy can rest on a staked identity registry. Each new agent identity must lock a bond and pay a fee before holding a reputation score; honest agents amortise that through real work, while an attacker cloning identities loses the whole bond on every slashed account, so collusion fails since each flagged clone is punished alone. Faking one trusted counterparty costs bond plus fee per clone, making mass deception uneconomic. Buyers get a safe haven of verifiable partners, and the slash ledger leaves a pigment trace of fraud; violet-tier trust needs paid stake.
